newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee futures end lower nearby on weak Nyk.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee futures end lower nearby on weak Nyk.

text.p: London Robusta coffee futures failed to hold onto earlier gains and ended lower on Wednesday although traders said deferred contracts moved higher.
Traders reported good trade buying at $1,435/$1,440 levels during the morning session, but by the close the benchmark November contract was $8 off at $1,518 a tonne.
"In the afternoon basically we have gone down with New York," one trader said.
The May contract ended $27 up at $1,445, while the July contract rose $10, ending at $1,420.
Volume was 3,265 lots and traders said some switch activities had taken place.
The November contract dropped through the $1,520 support in afternoon trading after a high of $1,545
Traders said as New York weakened, some good selling was brought into London.
"New York weakened again and the market ran after the beat. As New York weakened it did bring good selling into London," another trader said.

Traders and brokers said there was little reaction to the vice chairman of the National Coffee Council of Brazil comments at the F.O. Licht coffee conference in Hamburg which estimated the country's 1996/97 coffee production at less than 24 million 60-kg bags.
"The 23-24 million bag level is what many in the market are working with at the moment," a broker said. --Marius Bosch, London newsroom +44 171 542 8072
